newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's MIBANK to launch GDR soon.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's MIBANK to launch GDR soon.

text.p: Ten global securities houses are vying to be the agent for a global depositary receipt offering in Egypt's Misr International Bank/MIBANK expected to be launched soon, an official said on Wednesday.

The official, who refused to be named, told Reuters that the institutions started meeting representatives from state-owned Banque Misr, which owns 44.8 percent of MIBANK, this week to negotiate the size of the GDR. The state's Misr Insurance also owns four percent.

The state has decided to sell part or all of its stake in joint-venture banks, a move in line with the government's privatisation-led economic reform programme. It has already relinquished its majority in several other joint-venture banks.

The MIBANK offering will be the second GDR for an Egyptian bank and the country's fourth. Commercial International Bank GDRs are already trading in London as are Suez Cement and privatised al-Ahram Breweries.

The official named the 10 securities houses seeking to be lead managers for the bank issue as: Merrill Lynch, Nomura, Union Bank of Switzerland, Flemings, Paribas-Lehman Brothers, HSBC James Capel, Solomon Brothers, NatWest, BZW and ING Barings.

Banca di Roma has a 10 percent holding in MIBANK and Luxembourg-based Europartners Holdings owns 7.9 percent. Sakura Bank Ltd of Japan hold 2.6 percent, the British Arab Commercial Bank 8.5 percent and individuals own the remaining 22.2 percent.
The bank said it increased net profits for calendar 1996 to 141 million pounds ($41.5 million) from 95 million in the previous year.
The bank has a total of 3.75 million shares. The banking sector has helped the Cairo bourse rise to record highs in recent months and on Wednesday MIBANK shares were trading up at 780 pounds.
